## Day 2: Setting up an environment

Today we talked about reproducible environments with [Pixi](https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/workspace/environment/).

### Installing Pixi

```bash
wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
```

### Creating an environment

Run this once in the folder you're working in:

```bash
pixi init name_pixi_training -c conda-forge -c bioconda
```

This creates a `pixi.toml` file, which looks something like this:

```toml
[workspace] # <1>
channels = ["conda-forge", "bioconda"] # <2>
name = "name_pixi_training" # <3>
platforms = ["linux-64"] # <4>
version = "0.1.0"

[tasks] # <5>

[dependencies] # <6>
```

1. Overview section of the environment.
2. Channels: the sources we allow our tools and dependencies to come from.
3. The name of the environment.
4. The operating system the environment is optimised for.
5. Where tasks can be defined
6. The list of tools installed in the environment.

### The lock file

`pixi.lock` record of the channels and package source, license information, md5 checksums, and more.

::: {.callout-important}
Do not delete the `pixi.toml` or `pixi.lock` files. It breaks the environment, which will make you sad :(
:::

### Using the environment

Add a dependency with `add`:

```bash
pixi add quarto
```

Enter the environment:

```bash
pixi shell
```

Leave it again with:

```bash
exit
```
